commits.message: [Phase 0] Resolve all 9 open questions in emevo-diff.md against emevo source
commits.body:
Cloned emevo gecco2026 branch and verified all parameters against
config/env/20251122-predator-square.toml (the 960×960 predator-prey config).

Key findings that correct our previous assumptions:
- obs_dim = 205, not 54 (per-type sensor channels: 32×4 + 4×18 + 2 + 3)
- Velocity is 2D (vx, vy), not scalar speed
- energy_share_ratio = 0.4, not 0.5
- spawn_spread = 100.0, not 30.0
- Initial energy = 100.0 for both species, not 20/260
- Food capacity = 600 (body text correct), not 100 (Appendix A)
- Sensor range = 200 units (code), not 120 (paper)
- Network has 2 hidden layers, not 3
- Actions mapped via sigmoid_scale, not hard clipping

New deviation entries: D7 (obs layout), D8 (sensor range), D9 (network
depth), D10 (action mapping). D5 reversed (food=600).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Phase 0] Integrate phyjax2d, run_experiment.py, test_phase0.py; fix PPO JIT — 43/43 tests green
commits.body:
Sessions 5-6: Full integration layer and two critical performance fixes.

Core changes:
- environment.py: Replace step_physics() stub with real phyjax2d differential-drive
  physics. JIT-compiled 5-sub-step loop (lax.scan). dt=0.1, damping=0.8/0.6,
  5 sub-steps matching emevo gecco2026. Food excluded from phyjax2d (D11).
  Fixed proximity sensor bin placement to center-based (D12).
- scripts/run_experiment.py: Full 10-step simulation loop (AGENTS.md order).
  Batched policy inference via vmap + power-of-2 padding to avoid JIT recompile
  on every population change (D14). ~log2(max_pop) total compilations vs. one
  per unique agent count.
- tests/test_phase0.py: 11-test integration gate (world bounds, food regen,
  sensor contact, energy dynamics, birth probability, offspring policy, checkpoint
  roundtrip). All pass.
- src/ppo.py: JIT-compile per-minibatch gradient step via module-level cache (D13).
  Without this, jax.value_and_grad re-traces 40x per PPO update per agent;
  with 45+ simultaneous updates at step 1024 this caused 30+ min before first log.
  After fix: first compile 0.73s, subsequent calls 0.07s.
- docs/emevo-diff.md: Added D11 (food not in phyjax2d), D12 (sensor bin centers),
  D13 (PPO JIT), D14 (padded batch policy).
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Phase 0] Optimize step loop: numpy rollout + param stack cache + jnp.asarray in PPO
commits.body:
Three per-step performance improvements (no behavioral change):

1. Rollout buffer now uses NumPy arrays instead of JAX. Each step previously
   called buf.at[ptr].set() (creates a new JAX array) for 4 fields × n_agents.
   NumPy in-place assignment is ~20x faster (~1ms vs ~23ms at 45 agents).
   ppo_update calls jnp.asarray() at the start to convert before JAX ops.

2. Stacked policy params cache (_get_stacked_params / _update_param_slot).
   Previously rebuilt jtu.tree_map stack from scratch every step (~51ms).
   Now cached by agent-id tuple; rebuilt only when births/deaths occur.
   After PPO update, only the changed agent's slot is updated via .at[].set().
   Saves ~50ms on the ~99% of steps with no population change.

3. Removed redundant get_observation + policy_forward in PPO trigger.
   The computed last_value was discarded anyway (ppo.py hardcodes last_value=0.0).

Result: 317ms/step → ~116ms/step measured at 45 agents (~8.6 steps/s in
isolated benchmark); 4.4 steps/s measured in full loop at 87 agents (step 5000).
25k smoke test projected ~1.5-2h vs original ~6h estimate.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Phase 0] Vectorize observation computation in JAX — 6.4x speedup, GPU-ready
commits.body:
Replace per-agent Python observation loop with a single JIT-compiled JAX call
using vmap over observers + scatter-min for sensor binning.

New file: src/observations.py
  - compute_all_observations(): returns (max_agents, 205) for all agents at once
  - _single_proximity_agents/food: vmap over observers, scatter-min into 32 bins
  - _compute_wall_distances: fully vectorized raycast (no vmap needed)
  - _winner_take_all: argmin across 4 channels + inverse distance encoding
  - _single_tactile: vmap over observers, contact detection + bin assignment
  - All pure JAX — same code runs on CPU and GPU

Modified: src/environment.py
  - Added species/radii SoA arrays to physics dict (maintained on birth/death)
  - Added extract_obs_state(): extracts fixed-shape JAX arrays for JIT functions
  - Pads food_positions to (food_max, 2) with food_active mask

Modified: scripts/run_experiment.py
  - Observation loop replaced with extract_obs_state + compute_all_observations
  - Reward computation vectorized: single jnp.sum over all agents

Benchmark (120 agents):
  Old per-agent loop: 91.6ms
  New vectorized:     14.3ms (extract_obs_state) + ~0ms (JIT-cached JAX)
  Speedup:            6.4x on CPU; GPU: JAX part → ~0ms

Tests: 52 passed, 3 skipped (9 new vectorized obs tests + 43 existing)
Correctness: vectorized output matches reference within atol=1e-3
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Phase 0] Fix extract_obs_state .at[].set() anti-pattern — 14ms → 3ms
commits.body:
The energy loop was calling .at[slot].set() 150 times in a Python loop,
creating a new JAX array copy on each iteration. Fixed by collecting
slots/values into Python lists first, then doing one batch
.at[slots_array].set(values_array) call.
commits.author: Axel Browne

commits.message: [Phase 0] Vectorize check_eating() with NumPy broadcasting — 200ms → 0.4ms
commits.body:
Replace nested prey×food (90K iterations at 150 agents) and predator×prey
(7.5K iterations) Python loops with vectorized distance/angle computations
using NumPy broadcasting.

Key changes:
- Prey-food: compute (n_prey, n_food) distance matrix in one call,
  vectorize contact + FOV checks, deduplicate via nearest-prey assignment
  using np.argmin + np.bincount
- Predator-prey: compute (n_pred, n_prey) distance matrix, vectorize
  mouth range + angle checks, deduplicate via nearest-predator assignment
- Deduplication uses "nearest valid agent" instead of "first in list order"
  (scientifically equivalent — iteration order was arbitrary anyway)

commits.message: [Phase 0] Add SimState JAX pytree + conversion bridge (jax_state.py)
commits.body:
First step of fully-JAX simulation rewrite. SimState is a flax.struct
dataclass containing all simulation state as fixed-size JAX arrays:

- Agent SoA: is_active, species, agent_ids, ages, energies, reward_weights
  (all max_agents=500)
- Policy: stacked params + optimizer states (each leaf max_agents × param_shape)
- Rollout: obs/actions/rewards/etc (max_agents × 1024 × dim)
- Food: positions + active mask (food_max=600)
- Physics: phyjax2d stated + solver (already JAX pytrees)
- Meta: rng_key, step counter, next_agent_id

Two creation paths:
- init_simstate(config, rng_key): pure JAX initialization from scratch
- worldstate_to_simstate(world, config): bridge from old WorldState for testing

SimState is a proper JAX pytree (161 leaves) — can be passed through
jax.jit, jax.lax.scan, etc. Old code is completely untouched.

commits.message: [Phase 0] Add unified sim_step_core — JIT-compiled steps 1-9 (jax_sim.py)
commits.body:
Single JIT-compiled function covering the full simulation step except PPO:
  1. Vectorized observations (existing compute_all_observations)
  2. Batched policy sampling (vmap over all slots)
  3. Rollout buffer writes (JAX .at[].set)
  4. Physics step (phyjax2d via lax.scan)
  5. Eating detection (pairwise broadcast)
  6. Reward computation (vectorized)
  7. Energy updates
  8. Birth/death processing (vectorized probs + lax.scan spawning)
  9. Food regeneration

PPO (step 10) is returned separately — called from Python only for
agents with full rollout buffers. This avoids the vmap+lax.cond cost
of tracing both PPO branches for all 500 slots on every step.

Verified: 100 steps, no NaN, population growing (birth occurred),
food regenerating, energy correctly decaying. ~3 steps/s on CPU
at 13 active agents / 500 total slots.
